title.analysis: Authentic title "Do This Once You Have $50,000 Saved" is a milestone-trigger promise in a channel series ($20,000 and $100,000 versions are STRONG peers). The script delivers an ordered checklist (emergency fund, match, debt, Roth IRA, 401(k), HSA, index funds, automation), so the promise is honoured.

script.stored_text_completeness: All 16962 canonical characters read sequentially in full in 1 bounded ranges; auto-generated untimed text; stored ending is complete ("Don't be Alex."); ASR garbles ("Conaman" for Kahneman, "SPA scorecard" for SPIVA, "Mer" for Munger, "41k" for 401(k), "threeund" for three-fund); the Munger quote is censored or dropped; a character name is spelled both Jamie and Jaime; audio, timed delivery and editing unverified.
script.opening_words: Here's what nobody tells you about saving $50,000. You work toward that number for years. You skip things. You say no to things. You watch it climb from $12,000 to $19,000 to $31,000. And finally, finally, like it crosses $50,000 and for about 4 seconds, you feel incredible. And then immediately, like clockwork, a cold little voice in the back of your head goes, "Okay, but now what?" So, you do what any reasonable person does when they're overwhelmed by
script.ending_words: turn $50,000 into $500,000 are not smarter than Alex. They didn't get lucky on a stock pick. They just made a decision at the exact moment you're at right now when every instinct said, "Wait, be careful. Not yet." And they acted anyway, systematically, patiently, boringly. the emergency fund, the employer match, the Roth IRA, the 401k, the index funds, automated, left alone. That's the whole playbook. Don't be Alex.
script.analysis: Full 16962 canonical characters read. A single-narrator milestone checklist using two composite 30-year-olds (Alex leaves $50,000 at 0.01%, Jaime follows a framework): inaction cost and loss aversion, emergency fund in a high-yield account, employer match, high-interest debt, Roth IRA, extra 401(k), HSA, three-fund or target-date portfolio with SPIVA and the Buffett bet, behaviour gap (DALBAR, J.P. Morgan best days, Morningstar), a five-year Alex vs Jaime comparison, Munger quote, close. Most limits and arithmetic are right; the Buffett average, $500,000 match loss, $134,000 fee drag, VXUS fee and the five-year doubling are wrong or overstated.
beat_map: Loss aversion; inflation cost of inaction.
Step 1: emergency fund in a high-yield account; Santander 69%.
Index funds: SPIVA, Buffett bet, three-fund portfolio, fee drag.
Five years later: Alex vs Jaime.
